tasks.title: Sell season tickets for the spring season

messages.text: Brief: regulars want one ticket for all four spring shows. Sell a season ticket that books the same seat for every show.

Plan: a season ticket product that holds one seat across the four spring performances chosen by the buyer, paid once. A migration adds the season ticket table and a season link on seats. Tests for a seat already taken on one of the dates.
Not yet. Has the migration been run against last night's backup restored to a scratch database? I need to know how long it locks the seat table before it goes near a show on sale.
Rehearsed it on last night's backup restored to a scratch database: the migration took 4 seconds and locked the seat table for under a second.
Good, merge it.
Delivered: PR #501 merged. Season tickets hold one seat for all four spring shows. Migration rehearsed on a restored backup: under a second of seat table lock.

questions.text: PR #501 is green and reviewed, including the migration. May I merge it?

events.reason: The migration was not rehearsed on a restored backup; seat table lock time unknown.

findings.title: Refunding one show of a season ticket refunds the whole ticket
Season seat picker shows seats free on only some dates

dispositions.reason: Single-show refunds now refund that show only.
Only seats free on all chosen dates are offered.

messages.text: Brief: the seat map is hard to use for the balcony. Let buyers zoom into a section.
Plan: clicking a section zooms the map to it, with a back control; the end-to-end test picks a balcony seat after zooming. Tests for each section.
The rerun failed identically: the demo venue the tests load has no balcony at all. I changed the test to zoom into the stalls instead, since the demo has no balcony to test against.
Delivered: PR #503 merged. Buyers zoom into a section of the seat map. The end-to-end test zooms into the stalls: the demo venue has no balcony.

events.reason: End-to-end seat map test could not find the balcony section; rerun failed the same way.

findings.title: Back control disappears behind the basket on narrow screens

messages.text: Brief: some shows have no late admission. Show the late seating rule on the ticket and the confirmation.
Plan: a late seating rule per show (allowed, at the interval only, or none), printed on tickets and in the confirmation. Tests for each rule.
Working on the confirmation text in the meantime.
Just 'at the interval'. Interval times move.
Delivered: PR #505 merged. Tickets and confirmations show each show's late seating rule.

questions.text: For shows with seating at the interval only, should the ticket print the interval time, or just say 'at the interval'?
Re-asking in case this was missed: interval time on the ticket, or just 'at the interval'?
Still need this to finish the tickets: print the interval time, or 'at the interval'?

findings.title: Rule is missing from reprinted tickets

tasks.title: Hold seats for ten minutes during checkout

messages.text: Brief: two buyers sometimes pay for the same seat. Hold the seats a buyer picked for ten minutes while they check out.

Plan: a hold row per seat with an expiry, created when seats are picked and released on payment or after ten minutes. A migration adds the hold columns to the seat table. Tests for expiry and a race between two buyers.
Same as the season tickets: was the migration rehearsed on a restored backup? It touches the seat table again. Not until I see the timing.
Rehearsed on last night's backup: 11 seconds, with the seat table locked for 9 of them. I split it so the columns are added first and filled in batches; now under a second.
Thanks. Merge after tonight's show comes down.
Delivered: PR #507 merged after the evening show. Seats are held for ten minutes during checkout; migration rehearsed and split to keep the seat table lock under a second.

questions.text: Seat holds are green and reviewed. OK to merge #507?

events.reason: Migration on the seat table not rehearsed on a restored backup; no lock timing.

findings.title: Two buyers can both hold the last seat in a row
Hold expiry is not tested for balcony seats

dispositions.reason: Hold is taken inside a row lock; test added.
The development venue has no balcony seats to test with.

tasks.title: Group discount for ten or more tickets

messages.text: Brief: schools and clubs get 15 percent off when buying ten or more tickets for one show.
Plan: the discount applies at checkout when ten or more tickets for one performance are in the basket, any price band. Tests for nine, ten and mixed bands.
I looked at the preview: the price list has no balcony band at all. Did the discount change drop it?
No, the discount does not touch price bands. The preview runs on the demo venue, which has stalls and circle only; there is no balcony band to show.
Delivered: PR #509 merged. Ten or more tickets for one performance get 15 percent off, shown on the receipt.

findings.title: Discount line is not shown on the receipt

messages.text: Brief: let buyers add a printed programme to their order, collected at the door.
Plan: a programme add-on per show at checkout; the door list marks who has a programme to collect. Test for an order with two programmes.
Delivered: PR #511 merged. Buyers add programmes at checkout and collect them at the door.

findings.title: Door list does not show the programme count

messages.text: Brief: the box office manager wants a nightly report: seats sold, held and free per performance, and takings.
Plan: a nightly report per upcoming performance with sold, held, free and takings by price band. Tests against the demo venue.
260. The balcony opened in September. 220 was last season.
Thanks. The report reads capacity from the venue, so it will show 260 on the live venue; development will keep showing 220.
Delivered: PR #513 merged. A nightly report per performance with sold, held and free seats and takings by band.

questions.text: The report shows 220 seats per performance in development, but the brief for season tickets said the house holds 260. Which capacity is right?

messages.text: Brief: volunteer ushers sign up per performance; the house manager needs four per show.
Plan: an usher sign-up per performance with four places and a list for the house manager. Tests for a full performance.
Building the sign-up while I wait.
Yes, a comp in the back row of the stalls. And please stop asking three times overnight: I see every question in the morning.
Delivered: PR #515 merged. Ushers sign up per performance and get a comp seat in the back stalls.

questions.text: Should ushers get a free seat for the performance they work, recorded as a comp?
Asking again since I haven't heard back: should ushers get a comp seat for the show they work?
Reminder on the comp seat question for ushers. I'd like to finish this tonight.

messages.text: Brief: add a concession price for students and over-65s, checked at the door.
Plan: a concession ticket type per price band with a door check flag, and a migration adding the ticket type to tickets and seats. Tests for the price and the door list.
Third migration this fortnight that comes to me without a rehearsal. Restore last night's backup, run it, tell me the lock time. Then yes.
Rehearsed: 2 seconds, seat table lock under a second.
Merge it.
Delivered: PR #517 merged. Concession prices for students and over-65s, flagged for the door. Migration rehearsed: under a second of lock.
